sources.entry: herdtools7 - Where herd7, litmus7 and klitmus7 live, the tools that run a litmus test against the x86, Arm and kernel models.

summary.one_liner: herdtools7 is a tool suite for testing weak memory models, including the herd7 simulator and the litmus7 and klitmus7 runners for x86, Arm and kernel models.
summary.what_it_does: The suite contains herd7, a generic simulator for weak memory models. It includes litmus7, which runs litmus tests written as assembler programs for Power, ARM, AArch64 or X86 to check the memory model of the machine executing them. It also includes diy7, which generates litmus tests from concise specifications. Additional tools are mcompare7, for analysing run logs from both herd and litmus, and klitmus7, an experimental tool that runs kernel memory model tests as kernel modules. The README says herdtools7 is the successor of the diy tool suite and points to asllib/README.md for aslref documentation.
use_cases: simulate weak memory model behaviour of litmus tests
run litmus tests on x86, Arm or Power hardware
test kernel memory model with kernel modules
generate litmus tests from concise specifications
compare herd simulator output with litmus run logs
how_to_run: See file INSTALL.md for compilation and installation instructions.
stack: OCaml (implied by INSTALL.md build; not named in README)
Python (pip install of pre-commit for contributors)
notable: Covers simulation (herd7) and hardware execution (litmus7) of the same litmus tests
klitmus7 runs kernel memory model tests as kernel modules
diy7 generates litmus tests from concise specs
Successor to the diy tool suite
